A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EquiBench and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Content can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 19 LLMs, prompting comparisons, prediction-bias analyses, and CUDA case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds fine-tuning comparisons in Section 6.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same benchmark construction and labeling pipelines using CSmith/LLVM, TVM/TenSet, Stoke, and online-judge submissions with variable renaming. The new fine-tuning comparisons evaluate model variants without changing the proposed benchmark method.

E1.justification: Both retain 2,400 pairs across DCE, CUDA, x86-64, OJ_A, OJ_V, and OJ_VA, covering the same four languages. The added fine-tuning comparisons identify no additional dataset, domain, or evaluated task.

E2.justification: Section 6 adds comparisons between Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct and its LoRA-tuned version, and between DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B and the released SemCoder model. The original 19-model comparison and prompting-study comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new fine-tuning experiment uses Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct with LoRA for three epochs on 1,200 labeled examples. Existing category sample counts, accuracy metrics, zero-shot/four-shot settings, and prompts are unchanged. The new experiment's evaluation split is unspecified.

E4.justification: Section 6 adds analyses of whether supervised label-based fine-tuning and SemCoder training improve benchmark performance. The prediction-bias analysis moves from v2 Appendix A.1 to v3 Section 5.3 without substantive changes; the difficulty analyses and CUDA synchronization/hint case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both report statistical testing at alpha = 0.05 for the syntactic-similarity analysis. v3 adds point estimates for fine-tuning without introducing repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or new statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: New Section 6 results report Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct accuracy of 59.8% before and 63.2% after LoRA tuning, and 49.9% for DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B versus 54.9% for SemCoder. These are newly reported comparisons. Matched original accuracy, prompting, and bias tables have identical values.

T1.justification: The category-specific equivalence definitions remain unchanged. Additional discussion of CUDA rounding and general undecidability elaborates existing concepts without introducing or revising formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The central benchmark, automation, and difficulty claims remain. The introduction removes the categorical assertion that success cannot come from shallow memorization or token-level heuristics, and adds the broader assertion that any program-semantics question can be formulated as equivalence checking.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds interpretations of the modest fine-tuning gains, including limited learning signals from binary labels, and develops applicability arguments for coding assistants and compiler components. It also explains the six-category selection and expands future training directions. The labeling-noise limitations retain their substance.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit public code/dataset availability statement and repository address in the abstract. It documents the new fine-tuning model, LoRA use, three epochs, and 1,200 training examples. Existing construction details and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography removes Bender and Koller (2020); the remaining cited works match. Section 6 replaces the claim of being the 'first benchmark in this space' with describing the benchmark as 'a first step,' modestly revising novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Targeted edits revise the title from 'Understanding of' to 'Reasoning about,' rewrite portions of the introduction and discussion, and expand domain explanations. Prediction-bias discussion moves into the main results, appendix sections are renumbered, and acknowledgments are added. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 replaces an inequivalent condition-change example with an equivalent dead-code-removal example; Figure 5 shortens the code snippets. The bias summary moves from Table A1 to Table 3, the prompting table becomes Table 4, Figure 6 moves, and the appendix adopts two columns. The full bias table is relabeled Figure A1.

improvement.justification: v3 provides limited empirical follow-through to v2's training suggestions through the LoRA and SemCoder comparisons, adds code/data access information, and better aligns Figure 2 with the documented DCE construction. These improve support and clarity while preserving the original evidence. Missing evaluation-split and uncertainty details limit the strength of the new fine-tuning evidence, so the overall gain is modest.
